questions.question: Define mass communication. How does it differ from interpersonal and group communication?
questions.solution_html:
• 1. The Medium, Not the Message (Marshall McLuhan) electronic media exert a
  • profound influence on human behaviour, not through the messages they convey, but
  • through the sensory environment they create. 2. Reinforcement Theory (Joseph
  • Klapper) mass media primarily reinforces existing beliefs, values and social norms rather
  • than introducing significant change. 3. Narcotising Dysfunction (Lazarsfeld and
  • Merton) Exposure to a constant stream of information result in superficial awareness
  • without corresponding engagement.4. Catharsis Theory (Seymour Feshbach) media
  • serve as a psychological outlet, allowing individuals to purge aggressive/ antisocial
  • emotions through vicarious experiences. 5. Media as Windows on the World (Edward
  • Shils and David M White) democratise access to cultural content by making more of the
  • good accessible to more people. 6. Corruptive Effects (Fredric Wertham) media content
  • fosters materialism, antisocial behaviour and emotional desensitisation causing damage
  • to moral and social development.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
questions.final_answer: to moral and social development.
